brown adjective

also light brown, brownish, brunette, tawny, tan, sandy, sandy hair, hazel, hazel eyes, dark brown, bright brown, strawberry blond

classical

Traupman 251
Traupman 251, 252

fulvus

Other words

  • fuscus — dark brown

    also used · classical · Traupman 167, 251; Traupman 251: dark brown

  • spādīx

    also used · classical · Traupman 251; Traupman 251: bright brown; chestnut; hazel

  • brunneus

    also used · medieval · Traupman 251

    Traupman notes that brunneus is Germanic.

  • castaneus

    also used · Renaissance · M-O s.v. brown, citing Vives

  • brūnus

    also used · medieval · M-O s.v. brown

  • suffuscus, suffusca, suffuscum — brownish, light brown

    also used · classical · Tac. Agr. 12 (Lewis & Short); Andresian p. 50 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Tacitus uses it of British pearls (Lewis & Short); sub- softens fuscus. Andresian gives it for a pale brown or beige; Traupman 251 has flāvidus for beige.

See also colour.

SourcesJohn C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 251.

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. brown.

Lewis & Short: suffuscus

Anna Andresian, Vocabula Picta (2014), p. 50.
